classification.difficultyReason: Choose the relevant sum or product definition, apply the parity identities and simplify signs to compare h(-x) with h(x) or -h(x). The source explicitly supplies the proof strategy.

content.prompt:
By defining a function
$$h(x)=f(x)\times g(x)$$
or
$$h(x)=f(x)+g(x)$$
and then simplifying $h(-x)$, prove the following statements.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The sum of two odd functions is odd.

answer.worked:
Let $f$ and $g$ be odd, and define $h(x)=f(x)+g(x)$.
$$\begin{align*}h(-x)&=f(-x)+g(-x)\\h(-x)&=-f(x)-g(x)\\h(-x)&=-\bigl(f(x)+g(x)\bigr)\\h(-x)&=-h(x).\end{align*}$$
Hence the sum is odd.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The product of two even functions is even.

answer.worked:
Let $f$ and $g$ be even, and define $h(x)=f(x)g(x)$.
$$\begin{align*}h(-x)&=f(-x)g(-x)\\h(-x)&=f(x)g(x)\\h(-x)&=h(x).\end{align*}$$
Hence the product is even.

children.label: c
children.prompt: The product of two odd functions is even.

answer.worked:
Let $f$ and $g$ be odd, and define $h(x)=f(x)g(x)$.
$$\begin{align*}h(-x)&=f(-x)g(-x)\\h(-x)&=\bigl(-f(x)\bigr)\bigl(-g(x)\bigr)\\h(-x)&=f(x)g(x)\\h(-x)&=h(x).\end{align*}$$
Hence the product is even.
